metadata.title: Local On-Demand Delivery Marketplace Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: Explore how a local delivery marketplace would need to change when cities restrict vehicles, essential-goods supply becomes unreliable, courier employment law changes, or an emergency combines all three conditions.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: A consumer selects listed items from one merchant, pays the displayed basket and delivery fees, and receives the order from an available independent courier matched by distance and expected time. The marketplace assumes listed stock is broadly accurate, roads are usable, and courier work remains offer-based.
metadata.residualArchitecture: Instead of binding an order to one exact basket, one transport mode, one courier labor model, and one normal city state, the adapted design separates customer intent from replaceable items, delivery capability from vehicle and worker role, and service promises from current zone capacity. Policy can change eligible supply, substitutions, work obligations, and operating areas while the same order, evidence, money, and customer communication remain coherent.
metadata.note: These tests concern city policy, prolonged supply conditions, labor law, and emergency demand. They are broader than a single late order, unavailable menu item, or failed dispatch service.

source.title: Residues: Time, Change, and Uncertainty in Software Architecture
source.author: Barry M. O'Reilly

stressors.name: A city bans motorized delivery vehicles from its center during business hours
stressors.detection: Municipal orders, geospatial zone feeds, enforcement dates, courier vehicle profiles, route violations, delivery-time changes, and merchant access guidance.
stressors.attractor: Demand and merchants remain inside the zone, but the dominant courier and routing assumptions are illegal for much of the day. Treating all couriers as interchangeable produces rejected work, unsafe handoffs, missed promises, and sudden loss of central-city coverage.
stressors.businessReaction: Declare the restricted operating state, identify eligible walking, bicycle, cargo-bike, and transfer options, adjust service promises and fees, stage supply at boundary points, explain coverage to merchants and consumers, and prove compliance.
stressors.residue: Separate delivery capability from courier identity and vehicle. A versioned zone policy describes time, vehicle, load, access, handoff, safety, and permit constraints; dispatch resolves each order to an eligible capability chain, while routing and promises use the same current zone state.

impacts.effect: Predictable earning depends on matching each courier's actual transport capabilities to legal work.
Couriers receive work that is legal and feasible for their vehicle, location, and operating window.
Offer details include zone access, vehicle requirement, transfer point, load, and realistic route.
Promise adherence is segmented by operating zone, delivery capability, and handoff model.
Shows eligible work, access constraints, transfer instructions, and capability-specific earnings.
Manages supply as transport capabilities by zone instead of a single pool of nearby couriers.
Matches an order to eligible capabilities and supports controlled multi-courier handoff.
Plans routes using current vehicle, access, transfer, and time restrictions.
Maintains verified vehicle, permit, load, accessibility, and training capabilities independently from identity.
Owns capability-aware matching and zone operation with courier and city-operations teams.
Makes dense-city multimodal logistics and controlled handoff a marketplace benchmark.

stressors.name: A prolonged food shortage makes half of listed grocery inventory unavailable each evening
stressors.detection: Supplier notices, POS stock deltas, repeated item removals, substitution requests, consumer complaints, price movement, and merchant fill-rate trends.
stressors.attractor: Substitution becomes the normal fulfillment path rather than an occasional exception. A basket that names exact products cannot express the customer's underlying meal, dietary, allergy, budget, quantity, or urgency constraints, and repeated chat decisions make delivery uneconomic.
stressors.businessReaction: Capture what matters about the mission, verify current availability, propose safe and affordable alternatives, reserve the accepted basket, preserve price and allergen evidence, and let merchants or consumers intervene only when judgment is needed.
stressors.residue: Separate customer purchase intent from the merchant items that fulfill it. Each basket line can carry purpose, required attributes, forbidden attributes, quantity tolerance, price boundary, substitution authority, beneficiary, evidence, and expiry; fulfillment records every proposed, accepted, rejected, and supplied item without rewriting the original intent.

impacts.effect: A worthwhile local order is measured by fulfilling the customer's real need, not only matching the original SKU list.
Consumers can place an essential-goods order with clear substitution, budget, and safety boundaries.
Basket lines explain availability confidence and let the customer declare what a valid replacement means.
Merchant-caused cancellation separates failed intent fulfillment from a governed accepted substitution.
Adds mission-aware substitution preferences, evidence, approvals, and final-basket explanation.
Treats controlled replanning as part of reliable fulfillment instead of waiting for an order failure.
Stores intent, constraints, substitution authority, and price boundaries separately from chosen items.
Publishes current item attributes, evidence, availability confidence, and eligible alternatives.
Preserves the original basket and records every replacement decision through fulfillment.
Owns the intent and substitution experience with merchant catalog and order teams.
Makes trustworthy substitution and grocery-intent fulfillment a direct competitive standard.

stressors.name: A country classifies marketplace couriers as employees with scheduled hours and benefits
stressors.detection: Final labor law, court decisions, regulator guidance, payroll requirements, collective agreements, courier research, and operating-cost forecasts.
stressors.attractor: Open-ended offer acceptance is no longer the only supply model. The platform must schedule paid capacity, track contracted time and breaks, assign work fairly, meet minimum earnings and benefits, and still coordinate independent or partner supply in other markets.
stressors.businessReaction: Define supported worker relationships by market, schedule employee capacity, separate attendance from productive work, apply the correct pay and benefit obligations, preserve safety and worker voice, and expose the service and cost implications to marketplace control.
stressors.residue: Separate person, worker relationship, employer, market, contract, skill, scheduled capacity, attendance, availability, assigned work, productive event, compensation rule, benefit, tax, and payout. Dispatch consumes eligible capacity without owning employment semantics, while an auditable earnings ledger explains every obligation under the relationship in effect.

impacts.effect: Earnings confidence covers scheduled pay, benefits, breaks, assigned work, and transparent adjustments.
Couriers can understand and fulfill a scheduled employment commitment as well as offer-based work.
Pay explanation includes hours, assignments, minimums, benefits, expenses, tax, and corrections.
Earnings confidence is measured separately for each worker relationship and compensation model.
Adds schedules, attendance, breaks, benefit visibility, employment documents, and pay explanation.
Combines employee, independent, and partner capacity through one explicit capability and obligation model.
Plans committed capacity, attendance, breaks, incentives, and optional availability by worker relationship.
Explains scheduled pay, task earnings, guarantees, benefits, expenses, and corrections as separate components.
Records employment obligations and marketplace payouts in one auditable financial model.
Owns supported worker relationships with legal, payroll, dispatch, and worker-experience partners.
Makes labor-model adaptability and worker trust a marketplace operating benchmark.

stressors.name: A major flood closes roads while demand for food and medicine triples
stressors.detection: Civil-protection alerts, flood and road-closure feeds, pharmacy and grocery demand, courier safety signals, merchant inventory changes, and zone-level promise failure.
stressors.attractor: Ordinary nearest-courier and exact-basket optimization becomes unsafe and unfair. Essential intent competes with discretionary orders, available items change quickly, only some transport capabilities can cross each zone, and employee capacity carries different safety and pay obligations.
stressors.businessReaction: Declare emergency zones, protect couriers, prioritize agreed essential missions, publish honest service levels, replan baskets and routes, schedule eligible capacity, coordinate merchants and authorities, and keep customer remedy and worker pay explainable.
stressors.residue: No new structural change is required: zone and transport capability policy constrains safe routing, intent-based baskets support controlled essential substitutions, and the explicit worker-relationship model supplies scheduled capacity and emergency compensation. A shared operating state coordinates those existing decisions.

impacts.effect: Local-order trust includes honest prioritization and fulfillment during a city emergency.
Customers can express an essential mission and receive feasible options under the current zone state.
Checkout and tracking show emergency priority, accepted substitutions, capability handoffs, and changing promises.
Promise adherence is evaluated against the declared emergency service level and mission class.
Coordinates emergency zones, mission policy, capacity, safety, service levels, and cross-marketplace communication.
Reuses existing capability, intent, and worker policies to establish one governed emergency mode.
Shows affected demand, supply, inventory, zones, safety actions, and unresolved obligations in one control view.
Uses the existing zone-capability model to avoid unsafe roads and plan controlled handoffs.
Uses the existing intent model to fulfill essential needs with approved available alternatives.
Can operate the emergency through existing routing, supply, worker, and order contracts.
Makes safe emergency commerce and transparent prioritization a marketplace resilience benchmark.
